record.title: Confirmation reflects the successful submission
record.description: Figma shows sample contact values on the confirmation screen, and the design description states that the screen summarizes the successful submission. The submitted user's name and email should therefore replace the illustrative sample values after a successful response.
record.conclusion: Confirmation displays the actual submitted name/email pair, with Figma confirmation treatment; sample values are illustrative. Associated AFU elements: AFU-REQ-010 and AFU-AC-005.
record.rationale: This is an evidence-backed deduction from the confirmation's stated purpose and Work's submission flow. The requirements AFU gives the shared actual-pair deduction an agent_decision origin involving requirements, frontend, and backend; its separate greeting personalization is recorded only as a requirements analyst minor detail. Frontend/backend supporting documents agree on the actual pair.

sources.locator: Contact form behavior: confirmation is shown only after a successful response; confirmation behavior: preserve Figma content and styling.

record.title: Submission-volume bounds for unauthenticated form
record.description: The Work excludes authentication and requires storing each correctly submitted pair; duplicates are allowed and individual field lengths are bounded, but request frequency or total record volume was not specified. Unrestricted volume can affect resource consumption and availability, particularly if externally reachable.
record.conclusion: The product imposes no request-frequency or total-record limit. Continue accepting otherwise valid submissions and duplicates without an application-level volume cap; indefinite retention remains required. Physical capacity failures remain subject to the existing generic backend-failure behavior, and resource-growth feasibility is unverified. Associated AFU elements: AFU-RULE-006 and AFU-AC-004.
record.rationale: The human explicitly answered ‘I would not impose limits on request frequency or total record,’ resolving the observable policy. The requirements AFU carries this as a human_clarification origin; frontend and backend supporting documents agree. The human mandate authorizes the product-level unbounded behavior; finite physical capacity and operational availability remain unverified and are not recast as an application-level cap.

record.title: Retention rule for submitted contact data
record.description: The Work requires storing each name/email pair but did not state when records are deleted. The design reassures users that details stay private and secure but specifies no retention period. Indefinite retention versus a finite deletion period changes the data lifecycle and privacy posture.
record.conclusion: Retain each correctly submitted name/email pair indefinitely, with no time-based expiry or scheduled deletion, based on the human clarification. Associated AFU elements: AFU-RULE-005 and AFU-AC-003.
record.rationale: The human directly answered that records should be kept indefinitely. The requirements AFU carries this as a binding human_clarification origin; backend and frontend supporting documents agree. This does not establish manual deletion or infinite physical capacity.
